sections.h2: Which McIntosh County office answers a tax question?
sections.html:
Darien's North Way holds both tax offices. The assessors at number 601 appraise property and approve exemptions. At number 1200, in the county annex, the Tax Commissioner prints and mails statements and takes in what owners pay. The commissioner's own page states that it sets neither value nor millage.

McIntosh County numbers worth keeping by the phone (source: county website and Tax Commissioner site)

A house inside Darien may carry a city levy as well. State guidance gives billing of city tax to the city clerk, unless city and county agreed to merge the statements, so City Hall can tell you which applies.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about McIntosh County itself?
sections.html:
Marsh, tidal rivers and barrier islands define this county. The Census Bureau measures 574 square miles, and 150 of them are water. Darien started life as New Inverness in 1736, settled by Scottish Highlanders whom Oglethorpe had recruited, and the county separated from Liberty County in 1793. A British fort, Fort King George, went up in 1721. Federal troops burned Darien in June 1863. Following the Civil War, and until Georgia's disenfranchisement laws of 1907, McIntosh was a center of Black political strength, sending three Black representatives to the legislature between 1875 and 1907.

Besides Darien, the named places are Crescent and Eulonia, both census-designated places, with Townsend and Valona unincorporated. Sapelo Island is the most familiar of the islands. Liberty, Glynn, Wayne and Long counties are the neighbors, and Brunswick's metro area takes in the county.

  • Headcount: 11,989 in July 2025, a climb of 9.3 percent from 10,970 in 2020, though 2010 had counted 14,333.
  • Owners: 80.0 percent of households, living in homes worth $182,700 in the middle.
  • Tenants: $800 a month for the typical rental.
  • Older residents: 28.2 percent are 65 and over.
  • Pay and travel: households earn a median $50,273 and commute 37.5 minutes on average.
  • Room: 431.35 square miles of dry land, roughly 25 people on each in 2020.
  • Construction: 106 permits issued in 2025.

sections.h2: How does flood zoning change a McIntosh County sale?
sections.html:
Low coastal plains leave parts of McIntosh County and Darien open to river, canal and hurricane flooding, and the county names St. Catherine's, Sapelo, Doboy and Altamaha Sounds as contributors. Lenders ask about flood zones, so look yours up before listing.

Both the county and Darien participate in the federal flood insurance program. Regular homeowners coverage typically excludes flood, and a structure in a mapped high-hazard area with a federally backed mortgage must carry its own flood policy. Building and Zoning at 912-437-6603 looks up zones and base flood elevations and makes free site visits about flooding and drainage.

  • Under the county's 50 percent rule, repairs or renovations that raise a house's value by more than half require the lowest floor to be raised to at least base flood elevation when it sits below it.
  • In the AE and VE zones the underside of the lowest horizontal beam has to clear base flood elevation by one foot.
  • Suggested protection includes lifting electrical panels, heat pumps, water heaters and fuel tanks.

Marshes and low ground along the Darien, Altamaha and Butler rivers and Blackbeard Creek work as natural floodplains, per the county, that spread and absorb water, and that barrier islands such as Sapelo, St. Catherine's and Wolf blunt hurricane waves.

Call Building and Zoning before any pre-sale renovation, since the work itself can bring the elevation rules into play.

sections.h2: What payment dates and penalties does McIntosh County use?
sections.html:
The commissioner's site gives November 15, or 60 days after mailing, as the usual deadline and says that unpaid property can be levied upon and sold. State guidance counts the 60 days from the postmark and allows each county to choose its own official date.

Returns go in between January 1 and April 1. Without one, last year's return and value stand. An owner who thinks the value is wrong can file a return with their own estimate of market value, which protects appeal rights if the assessors raise it again.

Mobile homes follow a different clock. A home sitting in McIntosh County on January 1 needs tax and location permit settled by April 1, or the owner faces a 10 percent penalty, a Magistrate Court citation or a sale. To contest a mobile home value you have 45 days to reach the Board of Tax Assessors, and then 21 days from the notice to reach the Board of Equalization.

Send new mailing addresses to the assessor or commissioner quickly, since notices only go to the address on file.

sections.h2: How did the McIntosh County millage conversation go in 2024?
sections.html:
In September 2024 the county commission said it planned to collect 19.38 percent more than the rollback rate. The press release cited pay adjustments, a forecast 10 to 15 percent jump in employee health costs, inflation and the fact that millage had stayed flat for more than 15 years.

Because the rate exceeded rollback, state law called for three hearings, which the county held at Darien City Hall on September 26 and October 7, 2024.

For any later year, ask the County Commission Office for the adopted millage, and ask Darien City Hall for the city rate if the house is inside city limits.

sections.h2: Which McIntosh County exemptions and appeal rights matter before a sale?
sections.html:
The Tax Assessor's Office takes homestead applications, and new homeowners bring the warranty deed. A filing earns the current year's benefit only if it arrives by April 1, even though Georgia takes applications all year. Approval stays on the account until you move, sell or switch types, and a larger local exemption beats the state figure.

The commissioner's page describes a $2,000 standard exemption and elderly relief for incomes of $10,000 or less: up to $10,000 on school tax from age 62 and up to $4,000 on general tax from age 65. A floating exemption suits owners 62 and older with household income of $30,000 or less and replaces other state and county exemptions. A deferral for owners 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less delays tax until ownership changes or the debt hits 85 percent of value.

  • Qualifying farmland may be taxed on 30 percent of market value rather than 40.
  • Conservation use taxes eligible land on its actual use value.
  • Both programs bind the owner to a 10-year covenant.

Appeals of a real property value go to the Board of Tax Assessors, with a postmark inside 45 days of the notice's mailing.

sections.h2: What should a McIntosh County seller line up before closing?
sections.html:
Request each parcel's exact balance from the Tax Commissioner and ask the Assessor's Office whether a change in value or exemption is pending. Gather the flood zone and permit history before the sign goes up.

Deed recording triggers the state transfer tax: $1 on the first $1,000 and 10 cents on every additional $100, which the seller owes unless the contract assigns it to the buyer. The Clerk of Superior Court can speak to exemptions.

At the closing table, settle who covers the current-year bill, whether a lender has been paying from escrow, and when your exemption ends.

faqs.q: What is the McIntosh County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: The commissioner's site gives November 15, or 60 days after mailing. A mobile home is due April 1. Treat the date on your own statement as final.

faqs.q: Which McIntosh County office handles a disagreement over value?
faqs.a: The Board of Assessors at 601 North Way, 912-437-6663. The Tax Commissioner, 912-437-6627, sends bills and cannot change a value.

faqs.q: Can flood rules affect a McIntosh County house sale?
faqs.a: They can. A federally backed loan on a house in a Special Flood Hazard Area requires flood insurance, and the county's 50 percent rule may require raising the floor after major renovation.

faqs.q: What if a McIntosh County mobile home tax misses April 1?
faqs.a: Expect a 10 percent penalty, with a possible citation to McIntosh County Magistrate Court or sale of the home.

faqs.q: How does a McIntosh County owner apply for homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Apply at the Tax Assessor's Office, with the filing in by April 1 for that year. New homeowners bring the warranty deed.
